workflows..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: CI

# Fork policy: inherited from upstream and dispatch-only. It does NOT gate the
# fork's rail -- fork-ci.yml (macOS-first) does that. Kept dispatchable so a
# branch can be validated against a broader Linux/macOS matrix than fork-ci
# runs.
#
# The Windows jobs (windows-build-test, powershell-syntax, and the xwin
# cross-target check) were removed: this fork ships to macOS and Nix, publishes
# no releases, and does not test on Windows. See issue #19.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED: "true"
  # The fork has no DEPLOY_KEY secret; guard the ssh-agent steps so manual
  # dispatch works here while the file stays drop-in compatible upstream.
  JCODE_HAS_DEPLOY_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY != '' }}

jobs:
  quality:
    name: Quality Guardrails
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ssh-key: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
          submodules: recursive

      - name: Configure SSH for cargo git dependencies
        if: env.JCODE_HAS_DEPLOY_KEY == 'true'
        uses: webfactory/ssh-agent@v0.9.0
        with:
          ssh-private-key: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: quality-ubuntu
          cache-all-crates: "true"

      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: Check all targets and all features
        run: cargo check --all-targets --all-features

      - name: Run clippy with warnings denied
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

      - name: Enforce warning budget
        shell: bash
        run: scripts/check_warning_budget.sh

      - name: Enforce oversized-file ratchet
        shell: bash
        run: python3 scripts/check_code_size_budget.py

      - name: Enforce oversized-test ratchet
        shell: bash
        run: python3 scripts/check_test_size_budget.py

      - name: Run Rust production filter tests
        shell: bash
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_rust_production_filter.py'

      - name: Enforce panic-prone usage ratchet
        shell: bash
        run: python3 scripts/check_panic_budget.py

      - name: Enforce swallowed-error usage ratchet
        shell: bash
        run: python3 scripts/check_swallowed_error_budget.py

      - name: Enforce crate dependency boundaries
        shell: bash
        run: python3 scripts/check_dependency_boundaries.py

      - name: Enforce test env lease for config-fingerprint env vars
        shell: bash
        run: python3 scripts/check_config_env_lease.py

      - name: Enforce F20c retired distribution surface stays removed
        shell: bash
        run: scripts/f20c_removal_report.sh --stdout > /dev/null

      - name: Enforce wildcard re-export ratchet
        shell: bash
        run: python3 scripts/check_wildcard_reexport_budget.py

      - name: Enforce no unused dependencies
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cargo install cargo-machete --locked
          cargo machete

  build:
    name: Build & Test (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 35
    # Some dependencies (e.g. convert_case 0.10.0 via derive_more/crossterm, and
    # proc-macro2/quote) accidentally ship a `rust-toolchain.toml` *inside their
    # published crate*. When cargo builds such a crate its CWD is that crate dir,
    # so the rustup proxy honours the file: convert_case pins `channel = "1.83.0"`
    # and proc-macro2 requests `components = ["rust-src"]`. That made every
    # Build & Test job (a) race two parallel `rust-src` downloads and (b) later
    # try to compile convert_case with rustc 1.83.0, failing with E0514/E0599.
    # RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN takes precedence over any rust-toolchain.toml override, so
    # pinning it here makes every step use this job's installed stable toolchain.
    env:
      RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          - os: macos-latest
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ssh-key: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}
          submodules: recursive

      - name: Configure SSH for cargo git dependencies
        if: env.JCODE_HAS_DEPLOY_KEY == 'true'
        uses: webfactory/ssh-agent@v0.9.0
        with:
          ssh-private-key: ${{ secrets.DEPLOY_KEY }}

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}
          # Pre-install rust-src in the (serial) toolchain step. Some build-script
          # / proc-macro units trigger an on-demand `rustup component add rust-src`,
          # and when several parallel cargo/rustc processes request it at once they
          # race on the shared `~/.rustup/downloads/*.partial` file and fail with
          # "could not rename ... No such file or directory". Fetching it once here
          # removes the race. (Was failing every Build & Test job.)
          components: rust-src

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          # Suffix bumped to evict caches that held 1.83.0 / <unknown rustc>
          # artifacts produced before RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable pinned the job.
          key: ${{ matrix.os }}-stablepin

      - name: Install mold linker (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y -qq mold

      - name: Build
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p .cargo
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Linux" ]; then
            cat > .cargo/config.toml << 'EOF'
          [target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu]
          linker = "clang"
          rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold"]
          EOF
          fi
          # NOTE: intentionally NOT exporting RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache here. Only this
          # step used sccache while the later `cargo test --no-run` steps did not,
          # so sccache emitted rlibs/rmetas stamped `<unknown rustc version>` that
          # the non-sccache test compile then rejected with E0514
          # ("compiled by an incompatible version of rustc"). rust-cache already
          # caches target/ across runs, so a clean, wrapper-consistent build is
          # both correct and fast enough.
          RUSTC="$(rustup which rustc)"
          export RUSTC
          CARGO_BIN="$(rustup which cargo)"
          "$CARGO_BIN" build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Snapshot real home before tests (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        # Paired with the verify step after the test runs. Brackets rather than
        # assuming a clean HOME so the same gate works on a developer machine.
        run: |
          scripts/check_real_home_isolation.sh --snapshot

      - name: Compile library and binary tests
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 900 \
            "$(rustup which cargo)" test --target ${{ matrix.target }} --lib --bins --no-run

      - name: Compile integration test binaries
        shell: bash
        # Build the integration-test binaries up front (not counted against the
        # run steps' execution budgets). The e2e suite in particular is heavy
        # (burst-spawn concurrency), and folding compilation into its 900s run
        # budget was pushing slower hosted ubuntu/macos runners over the limit.
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 900 \
            "$(rustup which cargo)" test --target ${{ matrix.target }} \
            --test provider_matrix --test e2e --no-run

      - name: Run provider matrix tests
        shell: bash
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 600 \
            "$(rustup which cargo)" test --target ${{ matrix.target }} --test provider_matrix

      - name: Run e2e tests
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # e2e is fast (~1-2 min of execution); the generous budget only guards
          # against an occasional slow hosted runner. Compilation is already done
          # in the dedicated compile step above.
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 600 \
            "$(rustup which cargo)" test --target ${{ matrix.target }} --test e2e

      - name: Enforce real-home test isolation (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        # Cheap assertion, not a second suite: the test steps above already ran
        # in this job, so any test that resolved the real ~/.jcode instead of
        # its per-process temp home shows up as a delta against the snapshot.
        run: |
          scripts/check_real_home_isolation.sh --verify-only

      - name: Enforce warning budget (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          scripts/check_warning_budget.sh

      - name: Security preflight (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cargo install cargo-audit --locked
          scripts/security_preflight.sh --strict

  fmt:
    name: Format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt

      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
workflows..github/workflows/docs-impact.yml:
name: Docs Impact Advisory

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  review-packet:
    name: DOX Review Advisory
    continue-on-error: true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Build branch-wide DOX review packet
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          python3 scripts/docs_impact_advisory.py \
            --base "$BASE_SHA" \
            --head "$HEAD_SHA" \
            --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
workflows..github/workflows/fork-ci.yml:
name: Fork CI

# The fork's actual CI gate for `main`. This fork ships to exactly two
# surfaces: macOS/aarch64 (the maintainer's machines) and Nix (nix.yml).
# Upstream's ci.yml is inherited and dispatch-only. Windows CI was removed
# entirely (issue #19); Windows remains a runtime target but is untested here.
#
# Routing and tiering:
#   pull requests : Detect changes always runs; quality guardrails run for Rust
#                   or gate-input changes, while macOS and Linux tests run for
#                   Rust changes
#   push/schedule : quality guardrails, macOS build and test execution, and full
#                   Linux test execution run unconditionally
#   scheduled runs: repeat the same blocking Linux coverage weekly


on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    # Weekly repeat of the blocking Linux test coverage.
    - cron: "0 8 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: fork-ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Some published crates ship a rust-toolchain.toml inside the crate
  # (convert_case pins 1.83.0, proc-macro2 requests rust-src) and the rustup
  # proxy honours it per-crate CWD. RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN takes precedence, so keep
  # every blocking fork job on the repository's known-good toolchain.
  # (Inherited hard-won fix from upstream ci.yml; see the comment there.)
  RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: 1.96.0

jobs:
  # Branch protection must require "Detect changes". The conditional checks
  # "Quality Guardrails", "Build & Test (macOS)", and "Linux Tests" should be
  # removed from required checks or made optional because they may be skipped.
  changes:
    name: Detect changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      rust: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.rust || 'true' }}
      scripts: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.scripts || 'true' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        continue-on-error: true

      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
        id: filter
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          filters: |
            rust:
              - 'crates/**'
              - 'src/**'
              - 'Cargo.toml'
              - 'Cargo.lock'
              - 'rust-toolchain.toml'
              - '.cargo/**'
              - 'tests/**'
              - 'examples/**'
              - 'assets/**'
            scripts:
              - 'scripts/**'
              - '.apm/**'
              - '.jcode/**'
              - '.github/workflows/**'
              - '.github/scripts/**'
              - 'docs/agent-workflows.md'
              - 'docs/BRANCHING.md'
              - 'docs/NIX.md'
              - 'docs/SWARM_ARCHITECTURE.md'
              - 'docs/SWARM_TASK_GRAPH.md'
              - 'CONTRIBUTING.md'
              - 'RELEASING.md'

  quality:
    name: Quality Guardrails
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.scripts == 'true' || github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Verify pinned Rust toolchain coherence
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected="$RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN"
          toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^channel = "\([^"]*\)"$/\1/p' rust-toolchain.toml)"
          flake_version="$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*rustVersion = "\([^"]*\)";$/\1/p' flake.nix)"
          toolchain_refs="$(
            grep -hE '^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]+uses:[[:space:]]+dtolnay/rust-toolchain@[^[:space:]#]+[[:space:]]*$' \
              .github/workflows/fork-ci.yml .github/workflows/security.yml \
              | sed -E 's/.*dtolnay\/rust-toolchain@([^[:space:]#]+).*/\1/' \
              | sort
          )"

          check_version() {
            local label="$1"
            local observed="$2"
            if [ "$observed" != "$expected" ]; then
              echo "::error::$label pins '$observed'; expected '$expected'"
              exit 1
            fi
          }

          check_version rust-toolchain.toml "$toolchain_version"
          check_version flake.nix "$flake_version"

          pinned_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$toolchain_refs" | grep -cFx "$expected" || true)"
          stable_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$toolchain_refs" | grep -cFx stable || true)"
          total_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$toolchain_refs" | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')"
          other_refs="$(
            printf '%s\n' "$toolchain_refs" \
              | grep -vFx -e "$expected" -e stable || true
          )"
          canary_stable_count="$(
            awk '
              /^  latest-stable-canary:$/ { in_canary = 1; next }
              /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:$/ { in_canary = 0 }
              in_canary && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]+uses:[[:space:]]+dtolnay\/rust-toolchain@stable[[:space:]]*$/ { count++ }
              END { print count + 0 }
            ' .github/workflows/fork-ci.yml
          )"

          if [ "$pinned_count" -ne 4 ] \
            || [ "$stable_count" -ne 1 ] \
            || [ "$canary_stable_count" -ne 1 ] \
            || [ "$total_count" -ne 5 ] \
            || [ -n "$other_refs" ]; then
            echo "::error::unexpected dtolnay/rust-toolchain action inventory"
            printf 'expected: four @%s blocking refs and one @stable canary ref\n' "$expected"
            printf 'observed refs:\n%s\n' "$toolchain_refs"
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: fork-quality
          cache-all-crates: "true"

      # Inherited upstream code does not always pass `cargo fmt --check` under
      # the current stable rustfmt. Reformatting files this fork has never
      # touched would grow the fork diff for no benefit, so this gate runs the
      # full-tree check once but only *fails* when a flagged file is one this
      # fork modified relative to the `fork-point` tag. Drift confined to
      # untouched upstream files is reported and tolerated.
      - name: Check formatting (blocking for fork-touched files)
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin tag fork-point
          git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d \
            fork-point HEAD -- '*.rs' | sort -u > /tmp/fork-touched
          cargo fmt --all -- --check > /tmp/fmt-out 2>&1 || true
          grep '^Diff in ' /tmp/fmt-out \
            | sed "s|^Diff in $PWD/||; s|:[0-9]*:\$||" \
            | sort -u > /tmp/fmt-flagged
          bad=$(comm -12 /tmp/fork-touched /tmp/fmt-flagged)
          if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
            echo "::error::rustfmt diffs in fork-modified files:"
            echo "$bad"
            cat /tmp/fmt-out
            exit 1
          fi
          untouched_only=$(comm -13 /tmp/fork-touched /tmp/fmt-flagged)
          if [ -n "$untouched_only" ]; then
            echo "::warning::untouched upstream files fail rustfmt (not blocking):"
            echo "$untouched_only"
          else
            echo "cargo fmt clean across the whole tree."
          fi

      # Doubles as the Linux mergeability canary: everything (tests included)
      # must still type-check on Linux so fork patches stay upstreamable.
      - name: Check all targets and all features
        run: cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features

      # Same tolerance policy as the formatting gate (and it reuses
      # /tmp/fork-touched from that step): run clippy over the whole tree
      # without -D warnings so it completes, then fail only when a lint's
      # primary span lands in a fork-modified file. Hard compile errors are
      # already caught by `cargo check` above. Vendor lint debt under
      # --all-features (which upstream CI rarely reaches, its Format job
      # fails first) is reported as a warning instead of blocking.
      - name: Clippy (blocking for fork-touched files)
        run: |
          cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features --message-format=json \
            > /tmp/clippy.json
          jq -r '
            select(.reason=="compiler-message")
            | .message
            | select(.level=="warning" or .level=="error")
            | .spans[]?
            | select(.is_primary)
            | .file_name' /tmp/clippy.json \
            | grep -v '^/' | sort -u > /tmp/clippy-flagged || true
          bad=$(comm -12 /tmp/fork-touched /tmp/clippy-flagged)
          if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
            echo "::error::clippy lints in fork-modified files:"
            echo "$bad"
            jq -r '
              select(.reason=="compiler-message")
              | .message
              | select(.level=="warning" or .level=="error")
              | .rendered' /tmp/clippy.json
            exit 1
          fi
          untouched_only=$(comm -13 /tmp/fork-touched /tmp/clippy-flagged)
          if [ -n "$untouched_only" ]; then
            echo "::warning::untouched upstream files carry clippy lints (not blocking):"
            echo "$untouched_only"
          else
            echo "clippy clean across the whole tree."
          fi

      - name: Enforce warning budget
        run: scripts/check_warning_budget.sh

      - name: Enforce oversized-file ratchet
        run: python3 scripts/check_code_size_budget.py

      - name: Enforce oversized-test ratchet
        run: python3 scripts/check_test_size_budget.py

      - name: Enforce agent instruction contract
        run: python3 scripts/check_agent_instructions.py

      - name: Test docs impact advisory
        run: python3 scripts/test_docs_impact_advisory.py

      - name: Run Rust production filter tests
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_rust_production_filter.py'

      - name: Enforce panic-prone usage ratchet
        run: python3 scripts/check_panic_budget.py

      # Keeps the jcode-tui suite runnable in parallel: a test that mutates
      # process-global render state without the shared lock reintroduces the
      # cross-thread pollution that F28 removed, and would otherwise only show
      # up as an intermittent failure long after the fact.
      - name: Enforce jcode-tui render-lock discipline
        run: python3 scripts/check_tui_render_lock.py

      # A fixture that returns its env lease before its EnvVarGuard tears down
      # in the wrong order: exclusion is released while the environment is
      # still being restored, so the next test to take the lease has its
      # JCODE_HOME silently overwritten. This surfaced only after F28 restored
      # parallelism, and only on Linux, as an assertion naming nothing relevant.
      - name: Enforce env-lease drop order in test fixtures
        run: python3 scripts/check_env_lease_drop_order.py

      # Any `dirs::home_dir()` outside jcode-storage opts that call site out of
      # the test-harness redirect. This is the static half of the ambient-root
      # defense: check_real_home_isolation.sh catches writes into the real home,
      # and jcode-storage's own test proves the helpers redirect, but neither can
      # see a caller that never asks the helpers. That gap let memory logs, the
      # copilot machine_id, and the openrouter model caches write to the real
      # ~/.jcode with JCODE_HOME set, and let the model picker read the
      # developer's own usage history.
      - name: Enforce ambient filesystem roots route through jcode-storage
        run: scripts/check_ambient_roots.sh

      - name: Enforce swallowed-error usage ratchet
        run: python3 scripts/check_swallowed_error_budget.py

      # A6's zero-growth half. The three ratchets above bound the working tree
      # but not their own baselines, which are deliberately unprotected so that
      # routine tightening needs no maintenance window
      # (docs/fork/ideal-base/evidence/R07/integration-adjudication.md). This
      # step adds the per-domain critical-path ceilings that a baseline raise
      # must not be able to absorb silently, plus the repository high-water
      # marks that make the recorded trend one-directional.
      #
      # --expect-digest pins the scope, ceilings, targets, and repository marks
      # from here. Weakening any of them requires editing this workflow and the
      # checker, both protected governance paths, so it lands in a reviewed
      # maintenance window. Tightening needs neither edit: ceilings are
      # high-water marks, so a cleanup just opens headroom. Refresh the pin with
      # `python3 scripts/check_critical_path_budget.py --print-digest`.
      - name: Enforce critical-path zero-growth budget and report debt trend
        run: |
          python3 scripts/check_critical_path_budget.py \
            --expect-digest 2eafa153f1aca71934e356b16b1bae607d029b2f3e72313ba39aff7f2e2e56cf \
            --report /tmp/critical-path-debt-trend.json

      # R07's rereview-remediation established that a gate is only as good as
      # the tests that catch it being semantically neutered, and that those
      # tests must actually execute in CI. These assert domain attribution, that
      # the digest is sensitive to every field it claims to pin, that targets
      # are strictly downward, and that the pin above is not stale.
      - name: Test critical-path budget checker
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_critical_path_budget.py'

      - name: Upload critical-path debt trend report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: critical-path-debt-trend
          path: /tmp/critical-path-debt-trend.json
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-machete@0.9.2

      - name: Enforce no unused dependencies
        run: cargo machete

  governance-contract:
    name: Governance Contract Gate
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      # CI clones cannot contain the reviewed objects cited by STATE.json:
      # they are not ancestors of main; they live in local object stores and,
      # after R07 barrier 1, in the private recovery-archive repo. This opt-in
      # degrades only the reviewed-object existence check to a NOTE; every
      # other railway check stays strict, and existence is anchored by barrier
      # 1's fresh-fetch remote verification plus strict local validation.
      JCODE_RAILWAY_ALLOW_MISSING_REVIEWED_OBJECTS: "1"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Fetch published main explicitly
        run: git fetch --force --no-tags origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main

      - name: Reject shallow ancestry and validate governance/state
        run: |
          test "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository)" = false
          python3 -m unittest tests.test_ideal_base_railway
          python3 -m unittest tests.test_governance_compare
          python3 scripts/ideal_base_railway.py check \
            --published-ref refs/remotes/origin/main
          scripts/fork-health.sh \
            --fixture docs/fork/ideal-base/evidence/R07/fixtures/governance-valid.json \
            --fork-remote origin

  latest-stable-canary:
    name: Latest stable canary (advisory)
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    continue-on-error: true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      # Override the repository pin so this advisory job detects forward drift.
      RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: stable
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: latest-stable-canary
          cache-all-crates: "true"

      - name: Check all targets and all features on latest stable
        run: cargo check --locked --all-targets --all-features

      - name: Report latest-stable Clippy drift
        run: cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features

  macos:
    name: Build & Test (macOS)
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true' || github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0
        with:
          targets: aarch64-apple-darwin
          # Pre-install rust-src serially so parallel on-demand `rustup
          # component add` calls don't race on ~/.rustup/downloads (inherited
          # fix from upstream ci.yml).
          components: rust-src

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: fork-macos

      - name: Build release binary
        run: cargo build --locked --release --target aarch64-apple-darwin

      - name: Verify built binary launches
        run: ./target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/jcode --version

      - name: Compile library and binary tests
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 900 \
            cargo test --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin --workspace --lib --bins --no-run

      # Workspace coverage excludes jcode-tui and jcode-app-core because each
      # runs in an explicit blocking step with its own timeout attribution.
      - name: Run workspace library tests
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 900 \
            cargo test --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin \
            --workspace --lib --bins --exclude jcode-tui --exclude jcode-app-core

      # Parallelism restored by F28. The suite shares process-global TUI view
      # state (mermaid ACTIVE_DIAGRAMS, render/frame caches) and ambient env
      # (JCODE_HOME); every mutator now takes the shared render lock, enforced
      # by scripts/check_tui_render_lock.py, which fails the Quality Guardrails
      # rail if an unlocked mutator reappears. This was only ever a test-harness
      # concern, not a product race: the runtime is multi-process (each swarm
      # agent is its own OS process via the current_exe/spawn hook), so no two
      # live App contexts share this state. Verified green over 3 consecutive
      # full parallel rounds.
      - name: Run jcode-tui library tests
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 1800 \
            cargo test --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p jcode-tui --lib

      # Parallelism restored by F28. The env-toggling tests hold the
      # `lock_test_env` lease, which serializes exactly the cases that need it
      # instead of the whole suite. Verified green over 3 consecutive full
      # parallel rounds.
      - name: Run jcode-app-core library tests
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 1800 \
            cargo test --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin -p jcode-app-core --lib

      - name: Compile integration test binaries
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 900 \
            cargo test --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin \
            --test provider_matrix --test e2e --no-run

      - name: Run provider matrix tests
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 600 \
            cargo test --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin --test provider_matrix

      - name: Run e2e tests
        env:
          JCODE_E2E_REQUIRE_BINARY: "1"
          JCODE_E2E_BINARY: ${{ github.workspace }}/target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/jcode
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 600 \
            cargo test --locked --target aarch64-apple-darwin --test e2e

  linux-tests:
    name: Linux Tests
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true' || github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0
        with:
          targets: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
          components: rust-src

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          key: fork-linux-tests

      - name: Install mold linker
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y -qq mold clang

      - name: Configure mold linker
        run: |
          mkdir -p .cargo
          cat > .cargo/config.toml << 'EOF'
          [target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu]
          linker = "clang"
          rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold"]
          EOF

      - name: Compile library and binary tests
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 900 \
            cargo test --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --workspace --lib --bins --no-run

      # Workspace coverage excludes jcode-tui and jcode-app-core because each
      # runs in an explicit blocking step with its own timeout attribution.
      - name: Run workspace library tests
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 900 \
            cargo test --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu \
            --workspace --lib --bins --exclude jcode-tui --exclude jcode-app-core

      # Parallelism restored by F28; see the macOS jcode-tui step above.
      - name: Run jcode-tui library tests
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 1800 \
            cargo test --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -p jcode-tui --lib

      # Parallelism restored by F28; see the macOS jcode-app-core step above.
      - name: Run jcode-app-core library tests
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 1800 \
            cargo test --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -p jcode-app-core --lib

      - name: Compile integration test binaries
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 900 \
            cargo test --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu \
            --test provider_matrix --test e2e --no-run

      - name: Run provider matrix tests
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 600 \
            cargo test --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --test provider_matrix

      - name: Build jcode binary for e2e
        run: cargo build --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --bin jcode

      - name: Run e2e tests
        env:
          JCODE_E2E_REQUIRE_BINARY: "1"
          JCODE_E2E_BINARY: ${{ github.workspace }}/target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/debug/jcode
        run: |
          python3 .github/scripts/run_with_timeout.py 600 \
            cargo test --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --test e2e

  fork-ci-gate:
    name: Fork CI Gate
    needs: [changes, governance-contract, quality, macos, linux-tests]
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    env:
      CHANGES_RESULT: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
      RUST_CHANGED: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.rust }}
      SCRIPTS_CHANGED: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.scripts }}
      GOVERNANCE_RESULT: ${{ needs.governance-contract.result }}
      QUALITY_RESULT: ${{ needs.quality.result }}
      MACOS_RESULT: ${{ needs.macos.result }}
      LINUX_RESULT: ${{ needs.linux-tests.result }}
    steps:
      - name: Require every applicable Fork CI job
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          require_success() {
            if [ "$2" != success ]; then
              echo "::error::$1 concluded '$2'; expected success"
              exit 1
            fi
          }
          expect_routed() {
            local name=$1 applicable=$2 result=$3 expected
            case "$applicable" in
              true) expected=success ;;
              false) expected=skipped ;;
              *) echo "::error::$name has invalid routing value '$applicable'"; exit 1 ;;
            esac
            if [ "$result" != "$expected" ]; then
              echo "::error::$name concluded '$result'; routing requires '$expected'"
              exit 1
            fi
          }
          require_success "Detect changes" "$CHANGES_RESULT"
          require_success "Governance Contract Gate" "$GOVERNANCE_RESULT"
          quality_applicable=false
          if [ "$RUST_CHANGED" = true ] || [ "$SCRIPTS_CHANGED" = true ]; then
            quality_applicable=true
          fi
          expect_routed "Quality Guardrails" "$quality_applicable" "$QUALITY_RESULT"
          expect_routed "Build & Test (macOS)" "$RUST_CHANGED" "$MACOS_RESULT"
          expect_routed "Linux Tests" "$RUST_CHANGED" "$LINUX_RESULT"
workflows..github/workflows/fork-health.yml:
name: Fork Health

# Enforces the single-rail fork model invariants (see scripts/fork-health.sh):
# the fork-point tag still anchors main, and the rail exists. Runs daily and on
# demand. Drift opens/updates a single issue instead of failing silently. The
# live governance read requires RULESET_AUDIT_TOKEN because GitHub omits
# bypass_actors from callers without ruleset write access.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "37 9 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: fork-health
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  health:
    name: verify rail invariants
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Fetch the rail and tags
        run: git fetch --prune --tags origin main

      - name: Run fork health check
        id: health
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RULESET_AUDIT_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          scripts/fork-health.sh --live --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --fork-remote origin | tee health.txt
          {
            echo "## Fork health"
            echo '```'
            cat health.txt
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Open or update the drift issue
        if: failure()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          title="Fork health: rail invariant violation"
          run_url="${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
          existing="$(gh issue list --state open --search "in:title \"Fork health\"" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')"
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --body "Still violated: $run_url"
          else
            gh issue create --title "$title" \
              --body "scripts/fork-health.sh found rail drift. See $run_url and run it locally to reproduce." \
              --label fork-maintenance \
              || gh issue create --title "$title" \
                --body "scripts/fork-health.sh found rail drift. See $run_url and run it locally to reproduce."
          fi

      - name: Close the drift issue on success
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          existing="$(gh issue list --state open --search "in:title \"Fork health\"" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')"
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue close "$existing" --comment "Invariants hold again: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
          fi
workflows..github/workflows/freebsd-smoke.yml:
name: FreeBSD Smoke

# Builds and smoke-tests jcode inside a real FreeBSD VM.
#
# GitHub does not offer native FreeBSD runners, so we boot a FreeBSD guest
# (via QEMU) on a standard Ubuntu runner using vmactions/freebsd-vm. This runs
# the actual FreeBSD kernel and userland, giving a true build + run check
# instead of a cross-compile that can never link platform C dependencies
# (e.g. aws-lc-sys). See issue #416.

# Fork policy: manual dispatch only. The fork ships to
# macOS + Nix; FreeBSD coverage is upstream's concern. Run this by hand before
# sending a patch upstream that could plausibly affect FreeBSD.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release:
        description: Build in release mode (slower, matches shipping binary)
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: freebsd-smoke-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  smoke:
    name: FreeBSD Smoke (x86_64)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 120
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Build and test in FreeBSD VM
        uses: vmactions/freebsd-vm@v1
        with:
          release: "15.1"
          usesh: true
          # Give the build VM enough room: aws-lc-sys + tract pull in heavy C/Rust.
          mem: 6144
          cpu: 4
          # Install the toolchain jcode needs. The project is OpenSSL-free
          # (rustls + aws-lc-rs), so we only need a C/C++ toolchain, cmake, and
          # rust. pkgconf is handy for any transitive pkg-config probes.
          prepare: |
            pkg install -y rust cmake gmake pkgconf bash git
          # CARGO_BUILD_JOBS keeps memory in check; aws-lc-sys is memory hungry.
          run: |
            set -e
            echo "::group::Toolchain versions"
            uname -a
            cc --version | head -1
            cargo --version
            rustc --version
            echo "::endgroup::"

            export CARGO_TERM_COLOR=always
            export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3

            if [ "${{ inputs.release }}" = "true" ]; then
              PROFILE_FLAG="--release"
              TARGET_DIR="release"
            else
              PROFILE_FLAG=""
              TARGET_DIR="debug"
            fi

            echo "::group::cargo build (jcode binary)"
            cargo build --locked $PROFILE_FLAG -p jcode --bin jcode
            echo "::endgroup::"

            echo "::group::Verify binary launches"
            ./target/$TARGET_DIR/jcode --version
            echo "::endgroup::"

            echo "::group::Compile platform unit tests"
            cargo test --locked $PROFILE_FLAG -p jcode-base --lib --no-run
            echo "::endgroup::"

            echo "::group::Run platform unit tests"
            cargo test --locked $PROFILE_FLAG -p jcode-base --lib -- --nocapture platform
            echo "::endgroup::"
workflows..github/workflows/governance-root.yml:
name: Governance Root

# Audit gate: runs from the pull request head like any other workflow, so it
# detects an unreviewed governance-path change on the PR that makes it rather
# than preventing one. Legitimate governance-path changes go through the
# transaction-bound maintenance procedure in design.md section 4.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  governance-root:
    name: Governance Root
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Fetch the trusted main boundary
        run: git fetch --force --no-tags origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main

      - name: Detect governance-path changes
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          base="$(git merge-base HEAD refs/remotes/origin/main)"
          protected=(
            .github/scripts
            .github/workflows
            scripts/required-checks.json
            scripts/fork-health.sh
            scripts/ideal_base_railway.py
            tests/test_ideal_base_railway.py
            docs/fork/ideal-base/evidence/R07/github-governance.proposed.json
            scripts/ambient_roots_allowlist.txt
            scripts/check_agent_instructions.py
            scripts/check_ambient_roots.sh
            scripts/check_code_size_budget.py
            scripts/check_env_lease_drop_order.py
            scripts/check_panic_budget.py
            scripts/check_swallowed_error_budget.py
            scripts/check_critical_path_budget.py
            scripts/test_critical_path_budget.py
            scripts/check_test_size_budget.py
            scripts/check_tui_render_lock.py
            scripts/check_warning_budget.sh
            scripts/docs_impact_advisory.py
            scripts/rust_production_filter.py
            scripts/security_preflight.sh
            scripts/test_docs_impact_advisory.py
            tests/test_nix_distribution_policy.py
            tests/test_rust_production_filter.py
            scripts/governance_compare.py
            tests/test_governance_compare.py
            scripts/generate_governance_fixture.py
            docs/fork/ideal-base/evidence/R07/fixtures/governance-valid.json
          )
          if ! git diff --quiet "$base" HEAD -- "${protected[@]}"; then
            echo "::error::governance paths changed; use the recorded ruleset maintenance procedure (design.md section 4)"
            git diff --name-only "$base" HEAD -- "${protected[@]}"
            exit 1
          fi
workflows..github/workflows/nix-update.yml:
name: Update flake.lock

# Weekly dependency bump for the Nix flake inputs. Updates flake.lock on a
# temporary branch, validates the bump, and opens or refreshes a PR against
# `main`.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "47 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: update-flake-lock
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  update:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: main

      - name: Install Nix
        uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v31

      - name: Cachix (read-only public binary cache)
        uses: cachix/cachix-action@v17
        with:
          name: jerudnik-jcode
          skipPush: true

      - name: Update flake.lock
        id: update
        run: |
          cp flake.lock "$RUNNER_TEMP/flake.lock.before"
          nix flake update
          if git diff --quiet -- flake.lock; then
            echo "flake.lock is already up to date."
            echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Validate updated lockfile
        if: steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true'
        run: |
          nix build .#packages.x86_64-linux.jcode --dry-run --print-build-logs
          nix flake check --accept-flake-config --no-build --all-systems

      - name: Open pull request against main
        if: steps.update.outputs.changed == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          branch="automation/update-distro-flake-lock"
          body="$RUNNER_TEMP/update-flake-lock-pr.md"

          {
            echo "Automated weekly Nix flake input update."
            echo
            echo "### Changed inputs"
            jq -r --slurpfile before "$RUNNER_TEMP/flake.lock.before" '
              def label($locked):
                if $locked == null then
                  "none"
                elif ($locked.rev? // "") != "" then
                  $locked.rev[0:12]
                elif ($locked.ref? // "") != "" then
                  $locked.ref
                elif ($locked.version? // "") != "" then
                  $locked.version
                else
                  "unknown"
                end;
              .nodes as $after
              | $before[0].nodes as $beforeNodes
              | [
                  (($beforeNodes | keys_unsorted) + ($after | keys_unsorted) | unique[])
                  | . as $name
                  | ($beforeNodes[$name].locked // null) as $old
                  | ($after[$name].locked // null) as $new
                  | select($old != $new)
                  | "- \($name): \(label($old)) -> \(label($new))"
                ]
              | if length == 0 then ["- No lock input changes detected."] else . end
              | .[]
            ' flake.lock
            echo
            echo "### Validation"
            echo "- \`nix build .#packages.x86_64-linux.jcode --dry-run --print-build-logs\`"
            echo "- \`nix flake check --accept-flake-config --no-build --all-systems\`"
          } > "$body"

          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -B "$branch"
          git add flake.lock
          git commit -m "chore(nix): update flake.lock"
          git push --force-with-lease origin "$branch"

          existing_pr="$(gh pr list --head "$branch" --base main --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')"
          if [ -n "$existing_pr" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$existing_pr" \
              --base main \
              --title "chore(nix): update flake.lock" \
              --body-file "$body"
          else
            gh pr create \
              --base main \
              --head "$branch" \
              --title "chore(nix): update flake.lock" \
              --body-file "$body"
          fi
workflows..github/workflows/nix.yml:
name: Nix

# Builds, checks, and caches the jcode flake for the platforms this fork
# actually serves: x86_64-linux (CI validation + cache for Linux consumers)
# and aarch64-darwin (the maintainer's real machines). aarch64-linux was
# dropped deliberately -- no consumer exists; restore the matrix row when one
# does. Successful builds push to the public Cachix cache so downstream
# flakes never rebuild from source.
#
# flake.lock bumps live in nix-update.yml; cargo-audit policy in security.yml.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ["v*"]
    paths:
      - "flake.nix"
      - "flake.lock"
      - "nix/**"
      - "Cargo.toml"
      - "Cargo.lock"
      - "rust-toolchain.toml"
      - ".cargo/**"
      - "crates/**"
      - "src/**"
      - "assets/**"
      - "web/jcode-mobile/**"
      - "scripts/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - "apm.yml"
      - "apm.lock.yaml"
      - ".apm/**"
      - ".jcode/preferred-tools.md"
      - ".jcode/prompt-overlay.md"
      - ".jcode/swarm-prompt.md"
      - "README.md"
      - "CONTRIBUTING.md"
      - "RELEASING.md"
      - "docs/agent-workflows.md"
      - "docs/BRANCHING.md"
      - "docs/NIX.md"
      - "docs/SWARM_ARCHITECTURE.md"
      - "docs/SWARM_TASK_GRAPH.md"
      - "docs/ONBOARDING_SANDBOX.md"
      - "docs/WINDOWS.md"
      - "docs/WRAPPERS.md"
      - ".github/workflows/**"
  # Required context invariant: every pull request must instantiate Nix Gate.
  # Relevance controls may move inside jobs, but never back to workflow paths.
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: nix-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  validate:
    name: fast validation
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Install Nix
        uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v31

      - name: Cachix (read-only public binary cache)
        uses: cachix/cachix-action@v17
        with:
          name: jerudnik-jcode
          skipPush: true

      - name: Check workflow syntax (fork-owned workflows)
        # Only lint the workflows this fork owns. Upstream's ci.yml and
        # freebsd-smoke.yml are kept byte-close to the fork point and are
        # dispatch-only.
        run: |
          nix run nixpkgs#actionlint -- \
            .github/workflows/docs-impact.yml \
            .github/workflows/fork-ci.yml \
            .github/workflows/fork-health.yml \
            .github/workflows/security.yml \
            .github/workflows/nix.yml \
            .github/workflows/nix-update.yml \
            .github/workflows/release.yml

      - name: Dry-run Linux package
        run: nix build .#packages.x86_64-linux.jcode --dry-run --print-build-logs

      - name: Evaluate flake checks
        run: nix flake check --accept-flake-config --no-build --all-systems

      - name: Enforce Nix-only distribution policy
        run: nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.nix-distribution-policy --print-build-logs

      - name: Verify flake.lock is committed
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: |
          nix flake metadata --json > /dev/null
          if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain flake.lock)" ]; then
            echo "flake.lock is out of date; run 'nix flake update' and commit." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

  matrix:
    name: select build matrix
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      include: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.include }}
    steps:
      # Pull requests build + smoke-launch the real package (acceptance gate:
      # relevant path changes must run `nix build` and prove
      # `result/bin/jcode --version`). We restrict PRs to x86_64-linux: it is the
      # fork's CI validation platform, runs on fast hosted ubuntu, and reads the
      # public Cachix cache so it does not rebuild ~900 crates from source. The
      # full push/dispatch matrix additionally covers aarch64-darwin (the
      # maintainer machines) where cache misses are expensive on hosted macOS and
      # a per-PR rebuild is not worth the wall-clock cost.
      - id: pick
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            include='[{"system":"x86_64-linux","runner":"ubuntu-latest"}]'
          else
            include='[{"system":"x86_64-linux","runner":"ubuntu-latest"},{"system":"aarch64-darwin","runner":"macos-latest"}]'
          fi
          echo "include=$include" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build:
    name: build (${{ matrix.system }})
    needs: matrix
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.matrix.outputs.include) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 90
    env:
      CACHIX_CAN_PUSH: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) && secrets.CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN != '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Require Cachix publication for release tags
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ "$CACHIX_CAN_PUSH" != "true" ]; then
            echo "Tagged releases require CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN; Cachix is the sole binary publication channel." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Install Nix
        uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v31

      - name: Cachix (read/write public binary cache)
        if: env.CACHIX_CAN_PUSH == 'true'
        continue-on-error: ${{ !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') }}
        uses: cachix/cachix-action@v17
        with:
          name: jerudnik-jcode
          authToken: ${{ secrets.CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          # Main-branch cache upload is best-effort, but tag publication is a
          # release requirement. Push just the final result path rather than
          # relying on daemon post-job closure draining.
          useDaemon: false
          pathsToPush: ./result
          cachixArgs: -j2

      - name: Cachix (read-only public binary cache)
        if: env.CACHIX_CAN_PUSH != 'true'
        uses: cachix/cachix-action@v17
        with:
          name: jerudnik-jcode
          skipPush: true

      - name: Build package
        run: nix build .#packages.${{ matrix.system }}.jcode --print-build-logs

      - name: Smoke test binary (launch gate)
        # Prove the packaged binary launches. This is the F18 acceptance gate for
        # every build event, PRs included: we build the real package (doCheck
        # stays false -- the non-hermetic workspace suite is owned by ci.yml, not
        # the sandbox) and verify it actually runs.
        run: |
          ./result/bin/jcode --version

  release-metadata:
    name: publish metadata-only release
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: [validate, build]
    permissions:
      contents: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/release.yml

  nix-gate:
    name: Nix Gate
    needs: [validate, matrix, build]
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    env:
      VALIDATE_RESULT: ${{ needs.validate.result }}
      MATRIX_RESULT: ${{ needs.matrix.result }}
      BUILD_RESULT: ${{ needs.build.result }}
    steps:
      - name: Require validation and package build
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for pair in \
            "fast validation:$VALIDATE_RESULT" \
            "select build matrix:$MATRIX_RESULT" \
            "build:$BUILD_RESULT"; do
            name=${pair%%:*}
            result=${pair#*:}
            if [ "$result" != success ]; then
              echo "::error::$name concluded '$result'; expected success"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
workflows..github/workflows/release.yml:
name: Release metadata

on:
  workflow_call:

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release-metadata:
    name: Publish release notes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Verify tag belongs to authoritative main
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git fetch --no-tags "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git" main
          git merge-base --is-ancestor "${GITHUB_SHA}" FETCH_HEAD

      - name: Generate release notes
        run: scripts/generate_release_notes.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" > release_notes.md

      - name: Publish metadata-only GitHub release
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            assets="$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --json assets --jq '.assets | length')"
            if [ "$assets" -ne 0 ]; then
              echo "Release ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} already contains binary assets; refusing to publish metadata over it." >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
              --title "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
              --notes-file release_notes.md \
              --draft=false \
              --latest
          else
            gh release create "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
              --title "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
              --notes-file release_notes.md \
              --latest
          fi

          assets="$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --json assets --jq '.assets | length')"
          if [ "$assets" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Release ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} must not contain binary assets; Nix and Cachix are the sole binary authority." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

name: Security

# Fork security policy, in one place (was: a --strict preflight buried inside
# upstream's Build & Test job plus a permanently-green audit job in nix.yml).
#
#   secret scan    : secret patterns and script permissions on every push/PR.
#   dependency     : cargo-audit on main pushes and dependency-changing PRs,
#                    using the triaged ignores from .cargo/audit.toml. A NEW
#                    vulnerability fails this workflow -- and only this workflow,
#                    so unrelated work (Fork CI, Nix) stays green while you
#                    triage: either fix the dependency or add an ignore + a
#                    record to docs/security/advisories.toml in the same commit.
#   weekly report  : the full, un-ignored advisory picture (including triaged
#                    ignores and unmaintained/unsound warnings) posted to a
#                    single tracking issue, so accepted risk is re-reviewed on
#                    a cadence instead of rotting in the ignore list.
#
# Policy by advisory class (see docs/SECURITY_DEPENDENCIES.md):
#   direct vulnerability            -> dependency audit fails until fixed or triaged
#   reachable runtime transitive    -> dependency audit fails until triaged; weekly re-lists
#   build-time / non-compiled paths -> triaged ignore, weekly re-lists
#   unmaintained / unsound warnings -> advisory only (never --deny warnings)

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 9 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: security-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'weekly' || 'checks' }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  detect-dependency-changes:
    name: detect dependency changes
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      deps: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.deps }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
        id: filter
        with:
          filters: |
            deps:
              - 'Cargo.toml'
              - 'Cargo.lock'
              - '.cargo/**'
              - 'crates/**/Cargo.toml'

  advisory-policy:
    name: advisory ownership policy
    # Not gated on dependency changes: an acceptance expires with the calendar,
    # not with a diff, so this must be able to turn red on a PR that touches no
    # dependency and on the weekly schedule. Pure Python text checks, no build.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Every ignore is owned, documented, and unexpired
        # Structured ownership, not a grep for the ID in prose: every ignore in
        # .cargo/audit.toml must have a machine-readable record in
        # docs/security/advisories.toml carrying owner, rationale, affected
        # surface, expiry, and retirement condition. Undocumented, stale,
        # incomplete, and expired acceptances each fail here. CI evaluates
        # against the runner's date; preflight and the fixtures inject one.
        run: python3 scripts/check_advisory_policy.py

      - name: Policy fixtures (checker observed red and green)
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_advisory_policy.py' -v

  secret-scan:
    name: secret scan
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Security preflight (secret scan and permissions)
        run: scripts/security_preflight.sh

  dependency-audit:
    name: dependency audit
    needs: [detect-dependency-changes]
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule' && (needs.detect-dependency-changes.outputs.deps == 'true' || github.event_name != 'pull_request')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.96.0

      - name: Install Nix
        uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v31

      - name: Install cargo-audit (binary from nixpkgs, no compile)
        run: |
          nix build nixpkgs#cargo-audit --out-link "$RUNNER_TEMP/cargo-audit"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/cargo-audit/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Security preflight (secret scan, permissions, triaged audit)
        run: scripts/security_preflight.sh --strict

  weekly-report:
    name: full advisory report
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Install Nix
        uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v31

      - name: Run full cargo audit (no ignores)
        run: |
          set +e
          # cargo-audit auto-loads .cargo/audit.toml from the CWD; delete it in
          # this disposable checkout so triaged advisories reappear here for
          # scheduled re-review.
          rm -f .cargo/audit.toml
          nix run nixpkgs#cargo-audit -- audit > audit-report.txt 2>&1
          cat audit-report.txt
          {
            echo "## cargo audit (full, ignores disabled)"
            echo '```'
            tail -100 audit-report.txt
            echo '```'
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          # The report is informational; the tracking issue is the artifact.
          exit 0

      - name: Update the advisory tracking issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          title="Dependency advisories: weekly report"
          body_file="$(mktemp)"
          {
            echo "Weekly full \`cargo audit\` (ignores disabled). Triaged advisories live in \`.cargo/audit.toml\`, with owner, rationale, affected surface, expiry, and retirement condition in \`docs/security/advisories.toml\`."
            echo
            echo "Run: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}"
            echo
            echo '```'
            tail -100 audit-report.txt
            echo '```'
          } > "$body_file"
          existing="$(gh issue list --state open --search "in:title \"Dependency advisories: weekly report\"" --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')"
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue edit "$existing" --body-file "$body_file"
          else
            gh issue create --title "$title" --body-file "$body_file" --label fork-maintenance \
              || gh issue create --title "$title" --body-file "$body_file"
          fi

  security-gate:
    name: Security Gate
    needs: [detect-dependency-changes, advisory-policy, secret-scan, dependency-audit]
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    env:
      DETECT_RESULT: ${{ needs.detect-dependency-changes.result }}
      DEPS_CHANGED: ${{ needs.detect-dependency-changes.outputs.deps }}
      SECRET_RESULT: ${{ needs.secret-scan.result }}
      AUDIT_RESULT: ${{ needs.dependency-audit.result }}
      POLICY_RESULT: ${{ needs.advisory-policy.result }}
    steps:
      - name: Require every applicable security job
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [ "$DETECT_RESULT" = success ] || { echo "::error::dependency detection concluded '$DETECT_RESULT'"; exit 1; }
          [ "$SECRET_RESULT" = success ] || { echo "::error::secret scan concluded '$SECRET_RESULT'"; exit 1; }
          [ "$POLICY_RESULT" = success ] || { echo "::error::advisory ownership policy concluded '$POLICY_RESULT'"; exit 1; }
          case "$DEPS_CHANGED" in
            true) expected=success ;;
            false) expected=skipped ;;
            *) echo "::error::invalid dependency routing value '$DEPS_CHANGED'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$AUDIT_RESULT" != "$expected" ]; then
            echo "::error::dependency audit concluded '$AUDIT_RESULT'; routing requires '$expected'"
            exit 1
          fi
